artists.biography: Robert Clark "Bob" Seger (born May 6, 1945) is an American rock musician and singer-songwriter. After years of local Detroit-area success, recording and performing in the mid-1960s, Seger achieved superstar status by the mid-1970s and continuing through the 1980s with the Silver Bullet Band. A roots rocker with a classic raspy, shouting voice, Seger was first inspired by James Brown and Elvis Presley.[1] He wrote and recorded songs that dealt with blue-collar themes. Seger has recorded many rock and roll hits, including "Night Moves", "We've Got Tonight", "Like a Rock" and also co-wrote the Eagles number one hit "Heartache Tonight." His iconic signature song "Old Time Rock and Roll" was named one of the Songs of the Century in 2001. With a career spanning five decades, Seger continues to perform and record today. Seger was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Released in May 1978 on Capitol Records, Stranger in Town is the tenth studio album by Bob Seger and his second with the Silver Bullet Band. The album blends heartland rock, Detroit rock, and classic rock & roll, showcasing Seger’s signature storytelling and gritty vocals. Musically, it features a mix of hard-driving rockers and introspective ballads, with the Silver Bullet Band handling roughly half the tracks and the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section contributing to the rest, lending the album a rich, varied sound. Standout tracks include “Hollywood Nights,” “Still the Same,” “Old Time Rock and Roll,” and “We’ve Got Tonite,” all of which became staples in Seger’s live performances and enduring hits on classic rock radio.

Stranger in Town solidified Bob Seger’s status as a leading figure in American rock, following the breakthrough success of Night Moves. The album reached number four on the Billboard 200 and was certified six-times platinum, reflecting its massive commercial appeal. Critics praised its songwriting and production, highlighting Seger’s ability to capture the spirit of working-class life and personal longing. With its blend of energetic rock and heartfelt ballads, Stranger in Town remains a landmark release in Seger’s discography and a defining album of late-1970s rock.
